intent: Widen the sensor span from ±0.06 m to ±0.08 m (five sensors at 0.04 m spacing, the stated limit) and enlarge each footprint from 0.012 m to 0.016 m, so the tape is always bridged between neighbouring sensors. Sensor y stays at 0.05 and all other geometry is held fixed. Expected result: line_loss_events on the s-bend and slalom fall toward zero, max_error drops below 0.06 m, and the oval finish rate rises above 55%. Oval steering_oscillation is watched against the 0.25 threshold for the next step.
learning: Hypotheses: (1) The line losses at ±0.06 m come from drift beyond the outer sensors' reach, so ±0.08 m should remove most of them on the s-bend and slalom. (2) The 0.012 m footprint at 0.04 m spacing leaves a 28 mm gap wider than the tape, so it causes centre line losses. The 0.016 m footprint closes that gap. (3) Oscillation on the oval may rise with the wider array; if it passes 0.25 while losses fall, the next step is y 0.05 to 0.03. (4) If line losses are gone but rms_error stays above about 0.03, the 0.016 m footprint is too coarse, and the next step is to try 0.012 m with a 7-sensor array at about 0.027 m spacing. Please report per-track values so the slalom (highest max_error) can be checked separately.
rationale: Iteration 2 (±0.06 m span, 0.03 m spacing) scored 272.25, up from 129.96 at ±0.04 m. The oval finish rate is now 55%, with 0.35 line-loss events per run and max_error 0.049. The s-bend and slalom still fail: they show 0.6 and 0.95 line-loss events per run, with max_error 0.063 and 0.066, which is at the 0.06 m off-track floor. The Integrator's rule for persistent line loss at the limit is to widen the span to ±0.08 m at 0.04 m spacing, and that is the next step. The oval steering_oscillation of 0.267 is already above the 0.25 threshold, so the sensor-lead reduction (y 0.05 to 0.03) is also in play. I am not making that change yet. Moving the sensors closer to the axle would cut the look-ahead the controller needs on the sharpest bends, where the losses are concentrated, and changing it alongside the span would confound the result. I will hold y at 0.05 and read the oscillation in the next race. Sensor size also needs a change. At 0.04 m spacing with a 0.012 m footprint, the gap between neighbouring footprints is 28 mm, which is larger than the 25 mm tape. The tape can therefore sit between two sensors and be seen by neither, which causes line loss at the centre. A 0.016 m footprint leaves a 24 mm gap, which is always bridged by the tape, so at least one sensor always reads it. I keep five sensors so the Integrator does not need to change the array length. body_width, wheel, mass and body values stay unchanged because they are not limiting. Expected result: line_loss_events fall toward 0 on the s-bend and slalom, max_error drops below 0.06 m, and the oval finish rate rises. Possible costs are a coarser reading, which could raise rms_error, and oscillation above 0.25 on the oval.
